Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testEbeMultiplyMixedTypes()` calls `doTestEbeBinaryOperation(BinaryOperation.MUL, true)`, which tests the element-by-element multiplication (ebeMultiply) of RealVectors containing a variety of values, including NaN and infinity. The test expects correct element-wise multiplication results regardless of the values involved.

The current bug report points out a problem with `OpenMapRealVector.ebeMultiply(RealVector)` returning wrong values when the other vector contains NaN or infinity. Inspecting the `ebeMultiply` implementation shows the following logic:

- It first checks dimension compatibility.
- Then it creates a result vector `res` by copying this vector.
- It iterates only over the non-zero entries of the calling vector (`this`).
- For each non-zero entry, it multiplies the value by the corresponding entry in vector `v` and sets that in `res`.
- It does not explicitly handle entries where `this[i] == 0` but `v[i]` is NaN or infinity.

The submitted comment in the code (lines 368-372) acknowledges this limitation:
> The code assumes `0d * x = 0d` for any double `x`, therefore only non-zero entries of `this` are considered.
> This assumption is false when `this[i] == 0d` and `v[i]` is NaN or infinity, causing incorrect results.

Because the zero entries in the sparse vector `this` are not iterated or checked, any element where `this[i] == 0` and `v[i]` is NaN or infinity will not be updated in the result vector, leaving the result entry at zero instead of the mathematically correct NaN or infinity. This breaks the expected element-wise multiplication semantics and causes assertion failures in the test.

A similar implementation issue exists with `OpenMapRealVector.ebeDivide(RealVector)` which only iterates over the non-zero entries, missing important special cases per the comment in its code as well.

The failing test fails because:
- It tests elementwise multiplication of sparse and dense vectors with mixed special values.
- The sparse vector `OpenMapRealVector` assumes zero times anything is zero, skipping zero entries.
- This causes wrong results when multiplied by a vector containing NaN or infinity at positions where the sparse vector has zero.

In conclusion, the root cause of the bug is that the `ebeMultiply` method in `OpenMapRealVector` does not correctly handle zero entries in the sparse vector when the corresponding entry in the other vector is NaN or infinity. This leads to incorrect multiplication results and test failures.

The remedy would be to correctly handle the zero-entry cases in `ebeMultiply` by also iterating over all indices or at least special-casing these scenarios to produce correct NaN or infinity results.

No other recent bug reports provide more relevant information, so this diagnosis is focused on the current bug report and code snippets.

---

Next step: Suggest which methods are appropriate to fix based on this diagnosis.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
